messages:
maya.k: FYI support ticket #4521 — customer hit repeated 429s during our internal stresscheck. They ran a short burst test and then claimed auth errors and billing spikes. Can someone triage?

sam.c: I saw the alert. Their reported sequence: steady traffic -> sudden burst -> a bunch of 429s then some 502/504s. They gave curl repro in the ticket. Posting it here: `curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat -H \"Authorization: Bearer $KEY\" -d '{\"input\":\"hello\"}'` — headers show X-RateLimit-Remaining hitting 0.

liam: do we have the exact rate headers they saw? e.g. X-RateLimit-Limit, Remaining, Retry-After?

sam.c: yes — snippet from customer: `X-RateLimit-Limit: 120; X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0; Retry-After: 30` and after that some requests got 502s with `upstream read timeout` in our edge logs.

arun: hmm upstream read timeout suggests backend queue/backpressure. If requests pile up waiting for tokens, some routing might hit instance saturation and timeouts.

maya.k: reproduced locally with our latest staging key. Test harness: 5 keys, each doing 10 rps steady for 2m then a 45s burst at 60 rps per key. Result: edge returned 429s quickly, and after ~20s we saw 504s from model-host, and some requests failed auth briefly (401) for a subset — suspecting a rate-limit cache inconsistency between auth cache and quota cache.

liam: can you paste the minimal repro script?

maya.k: sure — here's the ramp script we used (bash + hey):

```
# ramp.sh
# 5 api keys in keys.txt, run hey per key in background
for k in $(cat keys.txt); do
  hey -q 1 -c 10 -z 2m -m POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $k" -d '{"input":"test"}' https://staging.redwood.ai/v1/chat &
done
# then after 2m, run burst for 45s
for k in $(cat keys.txt); do
  hey -q 1 -c 60 -z 45s -m POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $k" -d '{"input":"burst"}' https://staging.redwood.ai/v1/chat &
done
wait
```

arun: good. Observed behavior matches: token-bucket drained, edge replies 429, backend starts queueing and some requests exceed backend timeout. The auth 401s are odd — could be a race when auth cache refreshes and a bad token is briefly treated as expired. Need to check memcache invalidation traces.

sam.c: From support perspective, customer wants "sane defaults" for RPM/TPM and burst windows. Right now our per-key default is 120 RPM / 3000 TPM with a token bucket burst of 240 tokens (10s window). That clearly failed under their multi-key burst.

liam: Can we share the internal loadtest numbers we prefer for baseline? My suggestion: default per-key steady RPM = 60, TPM = 1200, burst capacity = 60 tokens (i.e., 1s equivalent at 60 rps) and short burst window 10s overall cross-key throttle. Also global account caps: 10 keys => throttle at account level to avoid N*burst.

maya.k: proposal sounds safer. But we need empirical backing. I ran a matrix: steady 60 rpm / key + 30s 10x burst (600 rpm) across 5 keys saturated edge but backend stayed stable with 95% success if burst cap per key = 60 tokens and global burst concurrency limited to 200 reqs. Without global cap we saw backend 504s.

arun: metrics we should capture: 429 rate, 5xx rate, mean latency p50/p95 during bursts, queue length on model-host, and auth-cache miss rate. Also capture X-RateLimit-* headers per response for debugging.

sam.c: action items for support: 1) share repro steps and recommend customers run staged bursts against staging to validate. 2) temporarily suggest lowering client concurrency while we tune defaults.

liam: eng tasks: 1) add memcache trace to auth path to see stale invalidate race. 2) add global burst defense in edge (simple semaphore) to clamp concurrent requests hitting model-hosts. 3) adjust default tokens: steady 60 RPM, 1200 TPM, burst bucket 60 tokens, token refill 1/s. 4) update docs and console recommended quotas.

maya.k: I've opened a small runbook in ops: `/runbooks/rate_limit_burst_escalation` (internal link). Quick notes added: how to reproduce, relevant logs, and rollback steps.

arun: small suggestion — use a leaky-bucket on the backend ingress in addition to token bucket to smooth spikes. That may reduce queue oscillation.

liam: agree. We'll prototype a soft-shed semaphore with circuit-breaker: if model-host queue > 100, return 429 with `Retry-After` to caller and emit metric.

sam.c: support update to customer queued: "We're running an internal calibration and will propose conservative defaults; recommended short-term mitigation: reduce your burst concurrency and add jitter to retries. We'll follow up with tuned settings." :thumbsup:

maya.k: timeline — auth trace by EOD, edge global cap POC tomorrow, defaults proposal doc by Friday. I'll file the RFC for console changes.

ops-bot: Deploy job finished: staging/edge v3.14 deployed (no downtime).

liam: thanks. Also let's add a test to our CI that simulates 5 keys with coordinated bursts so we don't regress.

maya.k: agreed — adding to nightly stresschecks. I'll post the updated test config once pushed.

sam.c: tagging @oncall in case someone sees alerts tonight.

liam: cool. filing follow-ups: ENG-1342 (global-burst-semaphore), ENG-1343 (auth-cache-trace), DOCS-78 (quota-defaults).

maya.k: closing loop: when defaults land we'll notify support to proactively reach out to customers who run self-tests.

sam.c: thanks all, good triage.
